children: U.S. corn fields appear to be showing yields that are even less than the cuts seen in September's WASDE report. "Early yield data has [us] wondering whether NASS [National Agricultural Statistics Service] will cut its U.S. corn yield forecast by another 2-3 [bushels per acre] in October," says AgResource in a note, adding that early harvest returns are showing "disappointing" results. In the September report, the USDA projected average corn yield at 178.5 bushels an acre--a forecast that may be even lower next month." CBOT corn is down 0.3%, while soybeans rise 0.3% and wheat falls 0.3%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
